findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: ioc_lookup_tool, payload_search_tool, fingerprint_search_tool, feint_sessions_tool · Private data: search_events_tool, ioc_lookup_tool, attack_timeline_tool, fingerprint_search_tool, fingerprint_similar_tool, fingerprint_population_tool, feint_credentials_tool, feint_files_tool, feint_sessions_tool · Public sink: search_events_tool, fingerprint_search_tool, fingerprint_population_tool, feint_files_tool · Destructive: asn_enrich_tool.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: ioc_lookup_tool, payload_search_tool, fingerprint_search_tool, feint_sessions_tool · Private data: search_events_tool, ioc_lookup_tool, attack_timeline_tool, fingerprint_search_tool, fingerprint_similar_tool, fingerprint_population_tool, feint_credentials_tool, feint_files_tool, feint_sessions_tool · Public sink: search_events_tool, fingerprint_search_tool, fingerprint_population_tool, feint_files_tool · Destructive: asn_enrich_tool

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "top_attackers_tool" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
